newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH UTILITIES' CREDIT QUALITY MAY WEAKEN - S&P.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH UTILITIES' CREDIT QUALITY MAY WEAKEN - S&P.

text.p: The credit quality of Finnish electricity utilities may weaken if they pile up a lot of debt to finance investments in new capacity and to buy distributors, rating agency Standard & Poor's said in a report on Wednesday.
"The industry's credit quality may be weakened if indebtedness is raised substantially to enable the utilities to participate in the industry's restructuring," it said.

Calling the current Finnish electricity distribution sector "fairly fragmented", S&P said consolidation was likely to continue although the number of distributors had already fallen by nearly 50 percent in the past 20 years.
"Borrowing needs of the electric utilities may increase due to investments in new capacity and purchase of independent distribution companies," S&P said.
But it also said "cost synergies can be gained from mergers between distributors, with economies of scale in electricity purchase, sales and marketing and information systems."

Finnish utilities may increase domestic power production capacity, partly due to the possibility that Sweden, having decided to phase out nuclear power, would be unable to export electricity, and partly because Russian contracts will expire.

S&P said electricity consumption was expected to increase in Finland but warned that electricity prices may turn more vulnerable when contract terms become shorter and electricity is traded on an exchange.

"However, increases in consumption and the reduction of Swedish supply from the nuclear phase-out could restrain downward pressure on market prices," it said. -- Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
